_comment: Diagnostics tsc reports when res/ecmascript/modules/** is type-checked
against generated/movian-api.d.ts. Enforced in BOTH directions by
check_reference_dts.py: an unlisted diagnostic fails, and a listed one
that stops firing fails too, so the list cannot quietly rot into a
This corpus is where a wrong native signature shows up first. Three
signatures that contradicted a real call site here shipped green through
the whole battery (movian#209) because nothing compiled these files.

`Duktape` used to be listed here as a recorded declaration gap. It is declared now (curated_interpreter_objects.json), the two diagnostics stopped firing, and the both-directions check refused to let the stale entries stay -- which is the half of this list that keeps it from decaying into a baseline.

`placeholder-callback` is gone too. It was never a fact about the declarations -- it was `this.onData = function() {}` inferring `() => void` from a no-op the module replaces at runtime. Declaring the placeholders with the handler signature they actually carry (movian#211) removed all four, so an accepted diagnostic turned out to be an annotation nobody had written.

Line numbers move when the modules gain comments, and movian#211's annotations moved all of them at once. That is the cost of pinning position: a re-baseline is a prompt to re-read the list, which is the opposite of what a count-only pin would have done -- there, a defect moving into a file that already had that code would have hidden.

private-instance-state.why: The calibration corpus declares the PUBLIC surface. State a constructor assigns for its own use -- Item.root, Item.page, NodeProto._gumboNode, Service.id, the videoscrobbler handlers -- is deliberately not declared; requiring it produces false positives from legitimate private state (settled in movian#137). The module reading its own private field is that decision, observed.

loose-var-redeclaration.why: `var i` declared twice in one function with different inferred types. ES5 var hoisting makes this legal and the module works; tsc is describing the module's own style, not the declarations.

duktape-proxy-handler.why: Duktape's Proxy predates the ES6 contract that `set` returns a boolean. The handler in movian/store.js returns void, which is what Duktape expects; lib.ES2015's ProxyHandler is the thing that does not match the runtime here.

buffer-coerced-to-string.why: `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f))` hands a buffer where tsc wants a string. Both sides are right: fs.readFileSync's `@returns {DuktapeBuffer}` describes what native/fs.read fills, and the module works because ES5 JSON.parse does ToString on its argument and a Duktape buffer coerces. TypeScript models no implicit coercion, so it reports what is genuinely an untyped step. Surfaced by movian#231, when the module's own @returns started being emitted -- before that readFileSync was `any` and the step was invisible. Wrapping the call in String() would silence it and is a production JS change, which #231 keeps out of scope.
